requirements.acceptance_condition: When distinct core, help, or extension material exists, provide a short reading route. Ordinary reading order suffices for a micro-explanation; do not create extensions or support sections merely to meet a template. No bold or italic prose in titles, headings, captions, tables, labels, code comments, or bibliography; conventional mathematical notation is allowed. In Markdown teaching prose, use plain paragraph labels rather than ATX/setext heading markup, bold markers, or italic markers. Exempt literal syntax inside code and conventional mathematical notation; do not exempt prose headings from the typography check. Check destination styling that can add emphasis without explicit markers, such as table headers. A different renderer's preview or absence of emphasis tags cannot verify this. When the destination forces bold or italic prose and its styling cannot be controlled, preserve the same information and relationships in a representation without that forced emphasis. Honour the requested format. Attempts, hints, and solutions must be reachable and correctly matched, with usable separation before answers are seen. For non-PDF notes, group hints apart from complete solutions with distinct labels and navigation when supported. Never interleave a hint with its full answer unless the user explicitly requests a combined worked solution rather than attempt help. In static PDFs use named links and return links; keep hints on different pages from full solutions and do not promise interactive reveals.
